newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch guilder seen bottoming out vs German mark.
newsitem.headline: Dutch guilder seen bottoming out vs German mark.

text.p: Dutch money market dealers said on Monday the guilder was not likely to weaken further against the mark, while market rates were expected to stabilise near the current level.
The guilder slipped to 112.46 per 100 marks this morning versus 112.44 on Friday.
"We have had the worst," one dealer said of the guilder/mark rate, adding that the guilder was seen bottoming out.
But another dealer said the Dutch currency should not be stigmatised as weak.
"It is all peace and quiet in the money market," the dealer said. "The current guilder/mark rate is not at all a disruptive factor."
Some money market dealers have said the rise of the Dutch special advances rate by 20 basis points to 2.70 percent on Thursday would support the guilder.
The guilder was lingering at 112.42 per 100 marks that day.
"The guilder could have been weaker today if the Dutch central bank had not decided on a rate rise last week," said one dealer.
Another dealer said the guilder was only somewhat late in reacting to the rate rise and it would regain ground in the near future.
Call money rates were stable at 2.88 percent bid and one-month deposits were bid at an unchanged 3.02 percent.
